prompt:
The following text is from Charlotte Brontë’s 1847 novel Jane Eyre. Jane, the narrator, works as a governess at Thornfield
Hall.
I went on with my day’s business tranquilly; but ever and anon vague suggestions kept wandering across my brain of
reasons why I should quit Thornfield; and I kept involuntarily framing advertisements and pondering conjectures about
new situations: these thoughts I did not think to check; they might germinate and bear fruit if they could.
Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: A. To convey a contrast between Jane’s outward calmness and internal restlessness
B. To emphasize Jane’s loyalty to the people she works for at Thornfield Hall
C. To demonstrate that Jane finds her situation both challenging and deeply fulfilling
D. To describe Jane’s determination to secure employment outside of Thornfield Hall
explanationEn:
Choice A is the best answer because it most accurately describes the main purpose of the text, which is to show that
while Jane calmly goes about her daily tasks, she is experiencing internal agitation about possibly seeking a new
job. At the start of the text, Jane says, “I went on with my day’s business tranquilly,” indicating that she is outwardly
calm. This outward calmness is then contrasted with her intense internal restlessness, as Jane says that thoughts
of leaving her job keep running through her mind, that she is “involuntarily framing advertisements” (meaning that
she can’t stop herself from thinking up potential listings for jobs), and that she often wonders what new “situations”
(or jobs) would be like.
Choice B is incorrect because the text gives no indication of Jane’s feelings, either positive or negative, about the
people she works for at Thorneld Hall. And rather than emphasizing that Jane feels particularly loyal to her
employers, the text focuses on her constant consideration of leaving her job. Choice C is incorrect because the text
gives no indication that Jane nds her current situation fullling, or satisfying. Given that much of the text is
focused on Jane’s thoughts about possibly leaving her job for a new one, it might be the case that she nds her
situation challenging, but there is no evidence in the text that Jane also nds that situation satisfying—she says
nothing positive about her current job at all, in fact. Choice D is incorrect because the text describes Jane as
wondering about getting a new job, not as determined to denitely do so. Jane keeps thinking about reasons why
she “should” quit her current job (indicating that she hasn’t yet decided to) and imagining possible new situations
she could nd, but she says at the end of the text that these thoughts “might germinate and bear fruit if they could,”
meaning that the thoughts haven’t yet led to a decision—that Jane isn’t yet determined to get a new job somewhere
else.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanationEn:

Quechua in her music. In this context, “inexperienced with” means not accustomed to. The text indicates that Flores
Rivera wanted to promote the Quechua language in her music and overcame a challenge by seeking help with

“Messy things,” said Marilla, whose aesthetic sense was not noticeably developed. “You clutter up your room entirely

noting that Anne “reveled in the world of color about her”—that is, she takes great delight in colorful things. It then
relates a scene when she enthusiastically enters the house with autumn foliage and announces that she will
decorate her room with it. The focus of the text then shifts to Marilla, who has an undeveloped “aesthetic sense,” or
appreciation of beauty, as can be seen when she dismisses the maple leaves as “messy things” and criticizes Anne
for cluttering her room with objects from outside. This episode thus illustrates that Anne and Marilla differ in their
appreciation of beauty and, more generally, in their basic character: Anne is exuberant and joyful, while Marilla is
stern and critical. Therefore, the purpose of the text is to show that Anne and Marilla have very different
personalities.
Choice A is incorrect because the text presents Anne’s appreciation of nature as a basic personality trait, not as a
newfound enthusiasm, and never indicates how recently she developed that appreciation. Choice B is incorrect.
Although the text portrays Anne and Marilla as having different personalities and attitudes toward natural beauty
and home decoration, it doesn’t show them engaging in an argument about this difference or suggest that they often
argue about it. Choice C is incorrect. Although the text does indicate that Marilla disapproves of how Anne plans to




decorate her room, Marilla’s disapproval is a supporting detail that serves to develop her personality, which the text
as a whole contrasts with Anne’s personality.

“deviates” would mean departs from an established course or norm. The text explains that the relationship between

prompt:
Interruptions in the supply chain for microchips used in personal electronics have challenged an economist’s assertion that
retailers can expect robust growth in sales of those devices in the coming months. The delays are unlikely to ______ her
projection entirely but will almost certainly extend its time frame.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanationEn:
Choice D is the best answer because it most logically completes the text’s discussion of the economist’s claim about
sales of personal electronic devices. In this context, “invalidate” most nearly means nullify or make invalid. The text
indicates that interruptions in the supply of microchips for personal electronics “have challenged” the economist’s
claim that sales of personal electronics will show strong growth in the coming months. The text goes on to clarify
the effect of the delays on the economist’s projection, stating that the delays are very likely to extend the time frame
over which the projected growth in sales will occur. This context suggests that the delays are unlikely to invalidate
the economist’s projection entirely—the delays will probably alter the time frame of the projection, not nullify it or
make it invalid.
Choice A is incorrect because saying that the delays are unlikely to “dispute,” or argue against, the economist’s
projection wouldn’t make sense. Since the delays are an inanimate circumstance, they couldn’t argue against a
prediction about the sales of personal electronics. Choice B is incorrect because saying that the delays are unlikely
to “withdraw,” or remove from consideration, the economist’s projection wouldn’t make sense. Although the
economist could withdraw her projection because of the delays, the delays themselves couldn’t withdraw her
projection since they’re an inanimate circumstance and thus can’t choose to remove something from consideration.
Choice C is incorrect because there’s nothing in the text to suggest that the delays will “underscore,” or emphasize,
the economist’s projection. Instead, the text suggests that the delays are likely to extend the time frame of the
economist’s projection but not to undermine the projection entirely.

Many studies in psychology have shown that people seek out information even when they know in advance that they have no

own sake.

think they can use it later. Dubey and colleagues acknowledge this fact (so they don’t claim people seek out

and colleagues’ study in Text 2. Neither text discusses the difculty of determining the motivation for information-
seeking. Choice D is incorrect. This choice contradicts Text 2, which starts with Dubey and colleagues
“acknowledging that acquiring information is a powerful motivator” (i.e., agreeing that curiosity explains the
seeking of apparently purposeless information). The research in Text 2 simply suggests that more than just

progression as a playwright can be considered to fall into three periods, with each one representing a particular thematic and

work across what Text 1 calls distinctive stylistic phases.

chronological progression supported in Text 1, but does not go so far as to say that Soyinka’s style remained
consistent. In fact, Text 2 points out “signicant differences in styles and content” among Soyinka’s plays. Choice C
is incorrect. Neither of the texts mention Soyinka’s poetry, nor do they rank his dramatic writing relative to his other




work. Choice D is incorrect. Neither text discusses the political aspects of Soyinka’s plays, nor do they make any
claims about whether they have changed over time.

Text 2

equipment from one another, especially when a species is known to exhibit other cooperative behaviors. At the same time, it
can be difficult to exclude the possibility that individuals are simply interested in the equipment because of its novelty,
curiously pawing or pecking at it until it detaches.

behavior of the magpies without trackers?

B. That behavior likely indicates that the magpies were deliberately attempting to benefit themselves by obtaining the
tracker.

C. That behavior may not be evidence of selflessness in Gymnorhina tibicen because not all the captured magpies

researchers’ perspective in Text 1 on the behavior of the magpies without trackers. According to Text 1, Dominique
Potvin and colleagues observed magpies without trackers pecking at a tracker on another magpie until the device
fell off. The researchers suggested that the birds might have been attempting to help the other bird, with no benet
to themselves. Text 2 generally discusses scenarios in which animals have been observed removing trackers from
each other. The text cautions that it shouldn’t be assumed that these animals are helping one another deliberately,
since they might simply be pecking at trackers out of curiosity, causing them to fall off eventually. Therefore, the
author of Text 2 would most likely respond to Potvin and colleagues’ perspective in Text 1 by saying that the
behavior of the magpies without trackers could be adequately explained without suggesting that they were
attempting to assist the other magpie.




Choice A is incorrect because Text 2 never discusses the novelty, or the newness and unusual quality, of the captive
settings in which animals have been observed to remove trackers from other animals, nor does it suggest that such
novelty might account for this behavior. Instead, the text suggests that it’s the novelty of the tracking equipment
itself that might cause the behavior: interested in the trackers because they’re unusual, animals might paw or peck
at them until they fall off. Choice B is incorrect because Text 2 never suggests that when animals remove trackers
from other animals, they do so because they wish to obtain the trackers for themselves. Instead, Text 2 argues that
animals paw or peck at trackers because they are merely curious about them. Choice C is incorrect because Text 2
doesn’t argue that when captured animals are observed removing trackers from each other, their behavior should be
regarded as seless only if all of them participate in it. Instead, the text argues that the behavior may not be seless
at all and may instead be attributed to animals’ curiosity about the new and unusual trackers.

Some foraging models predict that the distance bees travel when foraging will decline as floral density increases, but
biologists Shalene Jha and Claire Kremen showed that bees’ behavior is inconsistent with this prediction if flowers in dense

Choice A is incorrect because the text indicates that Jha and Kremen found that bees will behave differently than
some models predict if the bees encounter ower patches that are not rich in species, not if the owers are
“depleted,” or emptied or reduced in quality or quantity. Although it could be true that bees are likely to leave

and Kremen found that bees will behave contrary to some models’ predictions if the ower patches are not rich in
species. Choice D is incorrect because the text indicates that bees’ behavior will be inconsistent with the
predictions of some models if the ower patches that the bees encounter are of low species richness, not if the
owers are in patches that are “dispersed,” or widely scattered. Although the text does describe bees as leaving
patches that are not rich in species to forage elsewhere, there’s no suggestion that Jha and Kremen found that the

prompt:
While scholars believe many Mesoamerican cities influenced each other, direct evidence of such influence is difficult to
ascertain. However, recent excavations in a sector of Tikal (Guatemala) unearthed a citadel that shows ______ Teotihuacán
(Mexico) architecture—including a near replica of a famed Teotihuacán temple—providing tangible evidence of outside
influence in portions of Tikal.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanationEn:
Choice C is the best answer because it most logically completes the text’s discussion of architectural inuences
among Mesoamerican cities. In this context, “commonalities with” means similarities to or shared attributes with.
The text indicates that a recently discovered citadel in Tikal includes a close imitation of a famous temple in
Teotihuacán (another Mesoamerican city) and other evidence of Teotihuacán inuence, which suggests that the
citadel possesses features that resemble architectural features found in Teotihuacán. This context thus indicates
that the Tikal citadel shows commonalities with Teotihuacán architecture.
Choice A is incorrect because there’s nothing in the text that suggests that the Tikal citadel shows “renements of,”
or improvements on, Teotihuacán architecture. Although the text suggests that the architecture of Teotihuacán
inuenced the architecture of the Tikal citadel, and although it’s possible that later architectural designs could
make improvements on earlier designs, the text doesn’t discuss whether, in imitating Teotihuacán architecture, the
Tikal citadel’s builders improved on it. Choice B is incorrect because describing the citadel in Tikal as showing
“precursors of” Teotihuacán architecture—or features that preceded and foreshadowed those of Teotihuacán
architecture—would imply the opposite of what the text suggests about the relationship between the architecture
found in Tikal and Teotihuacán. The text claims that the discovery of similarities between the Tikal citadel and the
architecture of Teotihuacán, including a replica of a temple in Teotihuacán, provides evidence of outside inuences
on Tikal architecture. If the Tikal citadel was inuenced by Teotihuacán architecture, then the Teotihuacán
architecture must predate the citadel, not the other way around. In this context, therefore, it wouldn’t make sense to
say that the Tikal citadel shows precursors of Teotihuacán architecture. Choice D is incorrect because the text
discusses how the citadel in Tikal indicates the inuence of Teotihuacán architecture, which implies that the
makers of the Tikal citadel likely admired aspects of Teotihuacán architecture enough to imitate it. Thus, there’s no




reason to think that the Tikal citadel provides evidence of the Tikal people’s “animosities toward,” or feelings of
strong dislike or hostility toward, Teotihuacán architecture.

Microbes are tiny organisms in the soil, water, and air all around us. They thrive even in very harsh conditions. That’s why

prompt:
Text 1
The Cretaceous-Paleogene (K-Pg) mass extinction event is usually attributed solely to an asteroid impact near Chicxulub,
Mexico. Some scientists argue that volcanic activity was the true cause, as the K-Pg event occurred relatively early in a long
period of eruption of the Deccan Traps range that initially produced huge amounts of climate-altering gases. These
dissenters note that other mass extinctions have coincided with large volcanic eruptions, while only the K-Pg event lines up
with an asteroid strike.
Text 2
In a 2020 study, Pincelli Hull and her colleagues analyzed ocean core samples and modeled climate changes around the K-
Pg event. The team concluded that Deccan Traps gases did affect global conditions prior to the event, but that the climate
returned to normal well before the extinctions began—extinctions that instead closely align with the Chicxulub impact.
Based on the texts, how would Hull’s team (Text 2) most likely respond to the argument in the underlined portion of Text 1?
options: A. By agreeing that the Chicxulub impact changed the climate and that the Deccan Traps eruption caused the K-Pg event
B. By declaring that the changes in climate caused by the Deccan Traps eruption weren’t the main cause of the K-Pg event
C. By questioning why those scientists assume that the Chicxulub impact caused the Deccan Traps eruption

D. By asserting that the Deccan Traps eruption had a more significant effect on global conditions than those scientists
claim
explanationEn:
Choice B is the best answer because it describes how Hull’s team would most likely respond to the argument in the
underlined portion of Text 1, which asserts that volcanic activity in the Deccan Traps range led to changes in the
climate and caused the K-Pg mass extinction event. According to Text 2, although Hull’s team found that activity in
the Deccan Traps did indeed alter the climate before the K-Pg event, the team determined that the climate had
returned to normal before mass extinctions began. This nding and the observation that the K-Pg extinctions
closely align with the Chicxulub asteroid impact suggest that Hull’s team would likely dispute the claim in the
underlined portion of Text 1 and say that the climate changes caused by the Deccan Traps activity were not the
main cause of the extinctions.
Choice A is incorrect because Text 2 describes how Hull’s team found that the climate had recovered from the
changes brought about by the Deccan Traps activity before the K-Pg event occurred, which suggests that Hull’s team
would disagree that the Deccan Traps activity caused the K-Pg event. Additionally, the claim in the underlined
portion of Text 1 says nothing about how the Chicxulub impact changed the climate, so while Hull’s team might




believe that the impact did in fact change the climate, they could not be said to agree with the claim in Text 1 on this
point. Choice C is incorrect because there is no indication in either text that any scientists assume that the
Chicxulub impact caused the Deccan Traps activity, so there is no reason to conclude that Hull’s team would
question why the scientists referred to in Text 1 make such an assumption. Choice D is incorrect because Text 2
describes how Hull’s team found that the climate had recovered from the changes brought about by the Deccan
Traps activity before the K-Pg event occurred, which suggests that Hull’s team would say that the Deccan Traps
activity had a less enduring effect on global conditions than the scientists referenced in Text 1 believe, not that the
effect on global conditions was more signicant than those scientists claim.

The following text is adapted from Nathaniel Hawthorne’s 1844 short story “Drowne’s Wooden Image.” Drowne, a young man,
is carving a wooden figure to decorate the front of a ship.
Day by day, the work assumed greater precision, and settled its irregular and misty outline into distincter grace and beauty.
The general design was now obvious to the common eye.
As used in the text, what does the word “assumed” most nearly mean?

Choice A is the best answer because as used in the text, “assumed” most nearly means acquired, or came to possess.
The text portrays a character named Drowne carving a gure out of wood. At rst “irregular and misty,” or haphazard
and indistinct, the gure’s outline gradually showed “distincter grace and beauty” until the general design of the
carved object “was now obvious to the common eye,” or plainly recognizable to anyone. In other words, as Drowne
continued to carve, the wooden object came to possess, or acquired, greater precision, changing from an indistinct
outline or shape into a graceful, beautiful, and clearly recognizable form.
Choice B is incorrect. Although in some contexts “assumed” can mean acknowledged, or recognized, it doesn’t have
that meaning in this context because an inanimate object like the wooden gure can’t acknowledge its own
precision. Choice C is incorrect because there’s nothing in the text to suggest that the wooden gure merely
imitated, or mimicked, precision. Rather, the text suggests that as Drowne carved his wooden gure, it gradually
became more precise. Choice D is incorrect. Although in some contexts “assumed” can mean speculated, or
supposed based on incomplete information, it doesn’t have that meaning in this context because an inanimate
object like the wooden gure can’t speculate about its own precision.

Text 2

must also address strategies for higher-yield farming.

study?

the reported potential environmental benefits.

achieve meaningful results, whereas the author of Text 1 thinks the percentage is sufficient.

effect on biodiversity.

supplies."
Choice B is incorrect. This isn’t a difference between the two views. Text 1 does present the 15% number as enough to
achieve meaningful results, but that’s not what Text 2 takes issue with: rather, Text 2 argues that we need to
consider the effect that rewilding this much farmland would have on food supplies. Choice C is incorrect. This isn’t
a difference between the two views. Neither text mentions the timeline for achieving the results described by




Strassburg’s team. Choice D is incorrect. This isn’t a difference between the two views. Text 1 focuses on rewilding’s
effects on both carbon emissions and biodiversity. Text 2 doesn’t focus on rewilding’s effect on carbon emissions at
all. Instead, it focuses on a third factor: global food supplies.

Sugimoto moved from feudal Japan to the United States.
The standards of my own and my adopted country differed so widely in some ways, and my love for both lands was so
sincere, that sometimes I had an odd feeling of standing upon a cloud in space, and gazing with measuring eyes upon
two separate worlds. At first I was continually trying to explain, by Japanese standards, all the queer things that came

had in the United States using the standards ingrained in her from growing up in Japan. Thus, the main purpose of
the text is to convey the narrator’s experience of observing and making sense of the differences between two
cultures she embraces.
Choice B is incorrect because the text makes no reference to possible companions. Although the text does indicate

seemed to know” strongly implies that the narrator has interacted with other people in the United States, there is no
indication that these conversations involved her discussing Japanese customs. Choice C is incorrect because
nothing in the text suggests that the narrator was hesitant to ask questions. In fact, the narrator indicates that “no
one seemed to know the origin” of various customs, which provides evidence that, rather than being hesitant, she

distance between Japan and the United States. Although the narrator indicates that the two countries differ

Africa’s Sahara region—once a lush ecosystem—began to dry out about 8,000 years ago. A change in Earth’s orbit that

Neolithic peoples. He cites their adoption of pastoralism as a factor in the region drying out: the pastoralists’ livestock
depleted vegetation, prompting the events that created the Sahara Desert.
Text 2

subsistence likely didn’t cause the region’s desertification

contributed to the Sahara’s changing climate

Sahara region
explanationEn:
Choice A is the best answer. Brierley et al.’s research directly challenges Wright’s claim that pastoralism turned the

including pastoralism, could have contributed to the Sahara’s changing climate. In fact, their research implies that
the Neolithic peoples’ practices did not “exacerbate aridity” (i.e., make things worse), but may have slowed
environmental changes. Choice C is incorrect. Brierley et al.’s research does not acknowledge that pastoralism can
have deleterious (i.e., negative) effects on a region’s vegetation and climate. It only describes one possible benecial
effect: preserving vegetation through practices like selective grazing. Choice D is incorrect. Brierley et al.’s research

prompt:

point: In a 2014 study, Megan O’Brien and Alaa Ahmed had subjects stand or sit while making risky simulated economic
decisions. Standing is more physically unstable and cognitively demanding than sitting; accordingly, O’Brien and Ahmed
hypothesized that standing subjects would display more risk aversion during the decision-making tasks than sitting subjects
did, since they would want to avoid further feelings of discomfort and complicated risk evaluations. But O’Brien and Ahmed
actually found no difference in the groups’ performance.

O’Brien and Ahmed’s study.

of posture on cognition.

C. It explains a significant problem in the emerging understanding of posture’s effects on cognition and how O’Brien and
Ahmed tried to solve that problem.

posture on cognition.

Choice D is the best answer because it most accurately describes the main purpose of the text. The text notes that
although some studies have suggested that posture may have an effect on cognition, this phenomenon should not
be overstated. In other words, the text begins by urging caution and restraint when discussing the effects of posture
on cognition, implying that even though some studies have shown posture to affect cognition, we should not
assume that posture always affects cognition or does so in a strong way. The text goes on to discuss O’Brien and
Ahmed’s study as a "case in point" (that is, as an example of the point made previously). According to the text,
O’Brien and Ahmed hypothesized that since standing is more cognitively demanding than sitting, standing subjects
in their experiment would respond differently to decision-making tasks than sitting subjects would, which would
show an effect of posture on cognition. What the researchers actually found, however, was that the standing and
sitting subjects performed the same—posture did not affect cognition. By presenting a circumstance in which
posture does not appear to affect cognition, the discussion of O’Brien and Ahmed’s study shows why it is important
not to overstate the phenomenon. The purpose of the text, therefore, is to discuss O’Brien and Ahmed’s study to
illustrate why caution is needed when making claims about posture’s effects on cognition.




Choice A is incorrect because the text discusses O’Brien and Ahmed’s study as an example of why caution is needed
when discussing posture’s effects on cognition, not as an example of how research ndings related to posture and
cognition are often misunderstood. Although the text does warn against misunderstanding the scope of the
relationship between posture and cognition that has been reported in some previous studies, O’Brien and Ahmed’s
study is not one of those studies, and there is no suggestion that anyone has misunderstood O’Brien and Ahmed’s
ndings. Choice B is incorrect because the text makes no mention of the methods used in previous studies of the
effects of posture on cognition. Although the text does urge caution when discussing posture’s effects on cognition,
it does not critique the results of studies that suggested that posture can affect cognition. Instead, the text suggests

and Ahmed share that view or that they attempted to solve that problem. O’Brien and Ahmed are presented as

Conventional wisdom long held that human social systems evolved in stages, beginning with hunter-gatherers forming small
bands of members with roughly equal status. The shift to agriculture about 12,000 years ago sparked population growth that
led to the emergence of groups with hierarchical structures: associations of clans first, then chiefdoms, and finally,
bureaucratic states.
Text 2

socially flexible, alternately forming systems based on hierarchy and collective ones with decentralized leadership. The

seasonally, at times dispersing in small groups but also assembling into communities that included esteemed individuals.

Text 1?
options:
A. By conceding the importance of hierarchical systems but asserting the greater significance of decentralized collective

clan associations, then chiefdoms, and nally arriving at states with bureaucratic structures. Text 2 indicates that
Graeber and Wengrow believe that human social systems have been exible, shifting between different types of
structures, including both hierarchical and collective systems, and that these shifts may have even occurred
seasonally. This suggests that Graeber and Wengrow would dispute the idea that developments in social structures
have followed a linear progression through distinct stages.

collective societies are more signicant than hierarchical systems. Text 2 is focused on Graeber and Wengrow’s




view that humans have exibly shifted among various social structures, not on the importance of particular

Graeber and Wengrow believe that hierarchies didn’t emerge until after the rise of agriculture. In fact, Text 2

there’s no information in Text 2 suggesting that Graeber and Wengrow would challenge the assumption that

prompt:
The following text is adapted from Aphra Behn’s 1689 novel The Lucky Mistake. Atlante and Rinaldo are neighbors who have
been secretly exchanging letters through Charlot, Atlante’s sister.
[Atlante] gave this letter to Charlot; who immediately ran into the balcony with it, where she still found Rinaldo in a
melancholy posture, leaning his head on his hand: She showed him the letter, but was afraid to toss it to him, for fear it
might fall to the ground; so he ran and fetched a long cane, which he cleft at one end, and held it while she put the letter
into the cleft, and stayed not to hear what he said to it. But never was man so transported with joy, as he was at the
reading of this letter; it gives him new wounds; for to the generous, nothing obliges love so much as love.

upon receiving that letter.

begins by explaining how Charlot carefully delivers Atlante’s letter to Rinaldo, and then relates that Rinaldo feels
“transported with joy” after reading the letter. Therefore, the overall structure of the text is best described as a
description of the delivery of a letter followed by the portrayal of a character’s happiness after reading the letter.
Choice B is incorrect because the text indicates that the letter has been written; there’s no explanation why another
character hasn’t written one. In addition, the text’s description of Rinaldo “in a melancholy posture” suggests that
he’s sad and thoughtful, not that he’s desperate to receive the letter. Choice C is incorrect. Although the text states
that Charlot won’t toss the letter to Rinaldo because she doesn’t want it to fall, the text doesn’t refer to the contents
of the letter. Instead, the text describes how happy Rinaldo feels after reading it. Choice D is incorrect. Although the
text does describe Rinaldo’s reaction to the letter, the text doesn’t begin by discussing Atlante’s inspiration for

Astronomer Mark Holland and colleagues examined four white dwarfs—small, dense remnants of past stars—in order to

prompt:
Text 1
The fossil record suggests that mammoths went extinct around 11 thousand years (kyr) ago. In a 2021 study of
environmental DNA (eDNA)—genetic material shed into the environment by organisms—in the Arctic, Yucheng Wang and
colleagues found mammoth eDNA in sedimentary layers formed millennia later, around 4 kyr ago. To account for this
discrepancy, Joshua H. Miller and Carl Simpson proposed that arctic temperatures could preserve a mammoth carcass on
the surface, allowing it to leach DNA into the environment, for several thousand years.
Text 2
Wang and colleagues concede that eDNA contains DNA from both living organisms and carcasses, but for DNA to leach
from remains over several millennia requires that the remains be perpetually on the surface. Scavengers and weathering in
the Arctic, however, are likely to break down surface remains well before a thousand years have passed.
Which choice best describes how Text 1 and Text 2 relate to each other?
options:
A. Text 1 discusses two approaches to studying mammoth extinction without advocating for either, whereas Text 2
advocates for one approach over the other.

B. Text 1 presents findings by Wang and colleagues and gives another research team’s attempt to explain those findings,
whereas Text 2 provides additional detail that calls that explanation into question.

C. Text 1 describes Wang and colleagues’ study and a critique of their methodology, whereas Text 2 offers additional details
showing that methodology to be sound.

D. Text 1 argues that new research has undermined the standard view of when mammoths went extinct, whereas Text 2
suggests a way to reconcile the standard view with that new research.
explanationEn:
Choice B is the best answer. Text 1 introduces Wang and colleagues’ study and its surprising results, and then
mentions Miller and Simpson’s hypothesis as a possible way to explain them. Text 2, however, challenges Miller and
Simpson’s hypothesis by pointing out the difculties of preserving mammoth carcasses on the surface for
thousands of years: “scavengers and weathering” are the additional details that complicate the Miller/Simpson
hypothesis.
Choice A is incorrect. Neither text compares two different approaches for studying mammoth extinction. Text 1

unproductive ones

what constitutes productive behavior, giving the example that reading a book might be considered productive by
some but unproductive by others. It can be inferred that Maddux would also assert that whether watching TV or
playing games is productive or unproductive is a matter of subjective judgment. Thus, Maddux would most likely




caution against making an overly broad assumption, as there is no clear consensus in distinguishing between
productive and unproductive activities.

Text 2

the time that contributed to his theory on the importance of light. When working as an apprentice for a lighting specialist in

what was possible” with the elements of theatrical design.
Choice A is incorrect. Neither text describes how other lighting technicians responded to Appia’s ideas.
Furthermore, this claim isn’t relevant to Bremner’s evaluation of Appia’s technical expertise. Choice C is incorrect.
Neither text mentions anything about the opinions of theater practitioners who worked with Appia, so this answer
choice does not relate to the claim about Appia’s level of technical expertise made by Bremner in Text 1. Choice D is
incorrect. Neither text mentions anything about Appia’s familiarity with or ignorance of the use of music and sound
in theater. Both focus on his expertise (or lack thereof) in lighting.

Taming the forest and the prairie free;
No matter how we irrigate the sand,

should not interfere with nature. Rather, the speaker says that we are able to tame many different kinds of land, but
we are unable to tame the sea or beaches. Choice B is incorrect. This doesn’t describe the overall structure of the
text. The speaker never describes our cultivation, taming, and irrigation of land as “temporary.” Rather, the speaker
says that we are able to tame many different kinds of land, but we are unable to tame the sea or beaches. Choice C is
incorrect. This doesn’t describe the overall structure of the text. The speaker never describes our cultivation, taming,
and irrigation of land as an “admirable” approach to nature.” Rather, the speaker says that we are able to tame many
different kinds of land, but we are unable to tame the sea or beaches.

Fossils of the hominin Australopithecus africanus have been found in the Sterkfontein Caves of South Africa, but assigning
an age to the fossils is challenging because of the unreliability of dating methods in this context. The geology of Sterkfontein
has caused soil layers from different periods to mix, impeding stratigraphic dating, and dates cannot be reliably imputed
from those of nearby animal bones since the bones may have been relocated by flooding.
Text 2
Archaeologists used new cosmogenic nuclide dating techniques to reevaluate the ages of A. africanus fossils found in the

dating of the fossils there would be more accurate.

Sterkfontein Caves.

D. They would claim that cosmogenic nuclide dating is reliable in the context of the Sterkfontein Caves because it is applied
to the fossils directly.
explanationEn:
Choice C is the best answer. Text 2 states that the researchers used cosmogenic nuclide dating to "avoid the
potential for misdating" caused by the geology of Sterkfontein, which Text 1 describes as "challenging" and

A. africanus fossils have been "corrupted," but only that

Text 2. Text 2 agrees that stratigraphy and other methods are prone to error in the context of Sterkfontein: there’s a

Polar bears sustain themselves primarily by hunting seals on the Arctic sea ice, but rising ocean temperatures are causing
the ice to diminish, raising concerns about polar bear population declines as these large predators’ seal-hunting habitats
continue to shrink. A 2020 study examining polar bear populations across the Arctic concluded that populations affected by
sea-ice loss are at great risk of extinction by the end of the twenty-first century.
Text 2
Monitoring carried out by researchers from the Norwegian Polar Institute shows that the polar bear population on the Arctic
archipelago of Svalbard remains stable and well nourished despite rapidly declining sea ice in recent years. The researchers
attribute this population’s resilience in part to a shift in feeding strategies: in addition to hunting seals, the Svalbard polar
bears have begun relying on a diet of reindeer meat and birds’ eggs.
Based on the texts, how would the researchers in Text 2 most likely respond to the conclusion presented in the underlined
portion of Text 1?
options: A. By noting that it neglects the possibility of some polar bear populations adapting to changes in their environment

B. By suggesting that it is likely incorrect about the rates at which warming ocean temperatures have caused sea ice to melt
in the Arctic
C. By asserting that it overlooks polar bear populations that have not yet been affected by loss of seal-hunting habitats
D. By arguing that it fails to account for polar bears’ reliance on a single seal-hunting strategy
explanationEn:
Choice A is the best answer. Text 2 describes how the Svalbard polar bears have adapted to the loss of sea ice by
diversifying their diet and feeding on reindeer and seabird eggs, resulting in a “stable and well nourished”
population despite environmental challenges. This counters the underlined claim that polar bears facing a loss of
sea ice are at “great risk of extinction” by the end of the century.
Choice B is incorrect. Text 2 does not challenge the fact that sea ice is rapidly declining in the Arctic due to
warming ocean temperatures. In fact, it states that the Svalbard polar bears have faced “rapidly declining sea ice in
recent years.” Choice C is incorrect. The claim in Text 1 is specic to polar bear populations affected by the loss of
seal hunting habitats, so unaffected populations are irrelevant to the claim. Also, Text 2 doesn’t mention any polar
bear populations that haven’t yet been affected by loss of seal hunting habitats. It focuses on a population that has
been affected by sea-ice loss but has managed to survive and thrive nevertheless. Choice D is incorrect. Text 2
doesn’t imply that polar bears rely on a single seal-hunting strategy. In fact, the researcher in Text 2 would say that
Text 1 fails to account for polar bears’ ability to develop other hunting strategies and food sources.

introduces a contradiction to the one view presented at the beginning of the text. Choice D is incorrect. The text

birds. The paleontologists would nd that initial thought understandable, not confusing. Choice C is incorrect
because Text 1 never mentions lizards, so it wouldn’t make sense for the paleontologists in Text 2 to say that the

O. khaungraae must be a lizard. Choice D is incorrect. Although the

prompt:
Text 1
Films and television shows commonly include a long list of credits naming the people involved in a production. Credit
sequences may not be exciting, but they generally ensure that everyone’s contributions are duly acknowledged. Because they
are highly standardized, film and television credits are also valuable to anyone researching the careers of pioneering cast
and crew members who have worked in the mediums.
Text 2
Video game scholars face a major challenge in the industry’s failure to consistently credit the artists, designers, and other
contributors involved in making video games. Without a reliable record of which people worked on which games, questions
about the medium’s development can be difficult to answer, and the accomplishments of all but its best-known innovators
can be difficult to trace.
Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to the discussion in Text 2?
options:
A. By recommending that the scholars mentioned in Text 2 consider employing the methods regularly used by film and
television researchers

B. By pointing out that credits have a different intended purpose in film and television than in the medium addressed by the
scholars mentioned in Text 2

C. By suggesting that the scholars mentioned in Text 2 rely more heavily on credits as a source of information than film and
television researchers do

D. By observing that a widespread practice in film and television largely prevents the kind of problem faced by the scholars
mentioned in Text 2
explanationEn:
Choice D is the best answer because it reects how the author of Text 1 would most likely respond to Text 2 based on
the information provided. Text 2 discusses how the inconsistent use of credits to identify the contributors to video
games can pose an obstacle to scholars of the medium, who rely on such credits to answer questions about the
medium’s development. Text 1 notes that in lm and television, on the other hand, credits are used consistently and
are valuable to researchers studying the cast and crew members in these mediums. Since Text 1 asserts how the
consistent use of credits benets scholars of lm and television, it can be inferred that this text’s author would
respond to the discussion in Text 2 by observing that the kind of problem faced by scholars of video games—the
inability to know who contributed to a particular production and how—is, in lm and television studies, largely

prompt: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the warning raised in Text 1 regarding microplastic pollution in arable soil?
passage:
Text 1
Agricultural soils across the globe are accumulating alarming concentrations of synthetic polymer microplastics derived from degraded plastic mulch films. Ecologists caution that these microscopic fragments compromise soil bulk density and disrupt capillary water retention, threatening long-term crop yields.

Text 2
While the presence of microplastics in farmland is undeniable, soil microbiologist Dr. Elena Rostova discovered that indigenous soil mycorrhizal fungi and bacterial biofilms rapidly colonize microplastic surfaces. In controlled field trials, this microbial colonization aggregated soil particles into stable humus crumbs, entirely counteracting the porosity deficits predicted by laboratory simulations.
options: A. By arguing that microplastics actually improve nutritional content in commercial staple crops.
B. By suggesting that natural microbial processes may mitigate the negative structural impacts described in laboratory-based warnings.
C. By denying that plastic mulch films are currently utilized in commercial agricultural production.
D. By urging farmers to abandon organic composting in favor of chemical fertilizers.
explanationEn:
1. Text 1 warns that microplastics disrupt soil density and water retention.
2. Text 2 demonstrates that native soil microbes form biofilms that restore soil structure, counteracting the expected damage.
3. Therefore, Text 2 responds by suggesting that biological mechanisms can mitigate the structural degradation (Choice B).

2. This means the charcoal could have been pushed under the stones long after construction due to biological disturbance in the soil (Choice B).
3. Text 2 acknowledges the dates are 'technically accurate', eliminating A. It rejects the single-decade claim, eliminating C. Choice D is unrelated.

referenceFormula: \text{Bioturbation argument} \implies \text{Subsurface carbon deposited post-construction}

passage: For nearly a century, paleontologists operated under the consensus that sauropod dinosaurs held their long necks horizontally parallel to the ground to conserve metabolic energy. However, recent biomechanical reconstructions utilizing high-resolution computerized tomography and avian skeletal modeling indicate that sauropods maintained an elevated, nearly vertical neck posture similar to modern giraffes. By reinterpreting cervical vertebrae articulation, these findings have fundamentally altered prevailing conceptions of sauropod feeding ecology.
options: A. It outlines a long-standing scientific hypothesis, introduces new empirical findings that challenge it, and notes the broader impact of this revision.
B. It compares two competing computational models and concludes that both are insufficient to explain dinosaur physiology.
C. It describes an unprecedented technological breakthrough and chronicles its adoption across biological subfields.
D. It laments the loss of historic fossil specimens during computerized tomography scanning procedures.
explanationEn:
1. Sentence 1: Established consensus (sauropods held necks horizontally).
2. Sentence 2: Challenge based on new evidence (CT scans show elevated necks).
3. Sentence 3: Impact on feeding ecology.
4. Choice A precisely mirrors this progression: long-standing hypothesis -> challenging new findings -> broader implications.
explanationUz:
1. 1-gap: 100 yillik eski nazariya. 2-gap: Yangi kashfiyot uni rad etdi. 3-gap: Buning fanga ta'siri.
2. A variant bu strukturani mukammal ifodalaydi.
referenceFormula: \text{Structure: Consensus } \to \text{ Counter-Evidence } \to \text{ Paradigm Shift}

prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the second sentence within the overall text?
passage: Many economists anticipated that the introduction of automated checkout kiosks would cause immediate widespread layoffs across the retail grocery sector. However, empirical labor surveys over the subsequent five-year period revealed that overall employment levels in stores with automated kiosks remained steady, as companies redirected workers toward inventory logistics and customer assistance. Consequently, technological automation expanded operational capacity rather than terminating frontline personnel.
options: A. It introduces empirical counter-evidence that contradicts the forecast described in the preceding sentence.
B. It proposes a mathematical equation to measure store productivity metrics.
C. It laments the degradation of interpersonal communication in modern retail supermarkets.
D. It offers historical anecdotes regarding the invention of barcode scanners.
explanationEn:
1. Sentence 1 presents an expectation: kiosks would cause widespread layoffs.
2. Sentence 2 begins with 'However' and presents data showing employment remained steady.
3. Therefore, sentence 2 introduces empirical counter-evidence that directly refutes the initial forecast (Choice A).
explanationUz:
1. 1-gapda avtomatlashtirish ish o'rinlarini qisqartiradi degan bashorat aytilgan.
2. 2-gap 'However...' bilan boshlanib, real ma'lumotlar bu bashorat noto'g'ri chiqqanini ko'rsatgan.
3. A variant buni to'g'ri ifodalaydi.
referenceFormula: \text{Function: Counter-Evidence Refuting Initial Premise}

prompt: Which choice best describes the overall rhetorical purpose of the passage?
passage: Throughout the eighteenth century, European cartographers depicted Terra Australis Incognita as an immense temperate landmass counterbalancing the northern continents, populating their charts with speculative coastlines and fictional mountain ranges. When Captain James Cook's second Pacific expedition crossed the Antarctic Circle in 1773 without sighting land, it extinguished these Renaissance geographic fantasies. Cook replaced romantic conjecture with rigorous empirical navigation, definitively constraining any hypothetical southern continent to inaccessible polar ice.
options: A. It illustrates how empirical exploration dismantled speculative European cartographic myths regarding the southern hemisphere.
B. It argues that Renaissance cartographers possessed superior navigational instruments compared to eighteenth-century explorers.
C. It chronicles Cook's personal journals and their literary influence on European Romantic poetry.
D. It warns modern oceanographers against venturing into sub-zero Antarctic waterways.
explanationEn:
1. The text describes how cartographers imagined a fictional continent (Terra Australis), and Cook's empirical voyage disproved and replaced those myths with factual science.
2. Choice A accurately summarizes this rhetorical purpose.
explanationUz:
1. Matnda qadimiy xaritalardagi to'qima afsonalar Cookning amaliy ilmiy ekspeditsiyasi orqali puchga chiqarilgani aytilgan.
2. A variant to'g'ri.
referenceFormula: \text{Rhetorical Purpose: Replace Myth with Empirical Truth}

prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
passage: In 1915, Albert Einstein completed his general theory of relativity, postulating that gravity is not a Newtonian pulling force exerted instantaneously across void space, but rather the geometric curvature of spacetime deformed by mass and energy. When British astrophysicist Arthur Eddington observed the 1919 solar eclipse, he documented that starlight grazing the sun deflected exactly 1.75 arcseconds. By confirming this precise relativistic prediction, Eddington elevated Einstein from a respected theoretical physicist into a global scientific icon.
options: A. It outlines the historical trajectory that transformed an unverified hypothesis into globally celebrated scientific paradigm.
B. It concedes that Newtonian gravitational mechanics remains superior to general relativity in celestial navigation.
C. It refutes Eddington's empirical observations by demonstrating systematic astronomical measurement error.
D. It explains the specific mathematical formulas Einstein utilized to calculate spacetime curvature tensors.
explanationEn:
1. The text begins with Einstein's 1915 theory, details Eddington's 1919 eclipse verification, and concludes with Einstein's elevation to global renown.
2. The passage demonstrates how an abstract theoretical hypothesis was empirically verified and transformed into a celebrated scientific reality (Choice A).
3. Choices B, C, and D are factually inaccurate based on the text.
explanationUz:
1. Matn Eynshteynning nazariyasidan boshlanib, 1919-yildagi amaliy sinov va uning dunyo miqyosidagi tan olinishiga olib kelgan tarixiy jarayonni bayon qiladi.
2. A variant matnning umumiy ritorik maqsadini to'g'ri ifodalaydi.
referenceFormula: \text{Function: Theoretical hypothesis} \rightarrow \text{Empirical confirmation} \rightarrow \text{Global icon}

prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
passage: Although early critics dismissed Dr. Vance's unorthodox quantum decoherence hypotheses as fanciful conjecture, subsequent particle collision experiments conducted at CERN provided robust empirical evidence that _______ his theoretical framework.
explanationEn:
1. The sentence sets up a contrast ('Although early critics dismissed... subsequent experiments provided robust empirical evidence that...').
2. The second half must mean that the new evidence validated or confirmed the theory.
3. 'Corroborate' means to confirm, support, or give proof to an assertion (Choice B).
4. 'Obscure' (hide), 'dismantle' (destroy), and 'fabricate' (invent falsely) contradict the positive evidence.
explanationUz:
1. 'Although dismissed...' (Boshida rad etilgan bo'lsa-da) qarama-qarshiligi bor. Yangi tajribalar nazariyani TASDIQLAGAN bo'lishi kerak.
2. 'Corroborate' so'zi dalillar bilan tasdiqlash ma'nosini beradi.
referenceFormula: \text{Contrast Context: Dismissed } \iff \text{ Corroborated}

prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
passage: While philosophical treatises of the Enlightenment era often employed _______ arguments dense with esoteric terminology and circular rhetoric, Voltaire favored sharp satirical narratives written in plain vernacular to disseminate reformist ideals.
explanationEn:
1. The contrast compares Enlightenment treatises ('dense with esoteric terminology and circular rhetoric') with Voltaire's 'plain vernacular' and 'sharp' narratives.
2. The missing word must mean intricate, tangled, or excessively complicated.
3. 'Convoluted' means extremely complex and difficult to follow.
4. 'Transparent', 'succinct', and 'lucid' mean clear or brief, which are antonyms.
explanationUz:
1. 'dense with esoteric terminology and circular rhetoric' (murakkab, chalkash va aylanma) so'zlariga mos so'z kerak.
2. 'Convoluted' so'zi o'ta chalkash, chigal ma'nosini bildiradi.
referenceFormula: \text{Context Clue: Dense, Circular Rhetoric } \iff \text{ Convoluted}

prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
passage: Although the historical documentary presented a persuasive overview of urban planning initiatives, several civic historians faulted the filmmakers for omitting _______ archival testimony that directly contradicted the director's central thesis.
explanationEn:
1. The sentence states historians criticized the filmmakers for omitting testimony that 'directly contradicted the central thesis'.
2. The omitted evidence must be significant, prominent, or crucial.
3. 'Salient' means prominent, highly noticeable, or critically important (Choice B).
4. 'Peripheral' and 'inconsequential' mean unimportant; 'redundant' means repetitive.
explanationUz:
1. Tarixchilar film ijodkorlarini asosiy g'oyaga zid bo'lgan JUDA MUHIM dalillarni ataylab tushirib qoldirganlikda ayblashdi.
2. 'Salient' so'zi eng muhim, e'tiborga molik ma'nosini beradi.
referenceFormula: \text{Context: Contradictory Evidence Omitted } \implies \text{ Salient (Critical)}

prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
passage: While studying seismic spectrograms along the Cascadia subduction zone, geophysicists detected an _______ low-frequency tremor that deviated markedly from normal tectonic tremors, prompting an immediate deployment of sea-floor pressure gauges.
explanationEn:
1. The clue states the tremor 'deviated markedly from normal tectonic tremors'.
2. The missing word must mean abnormal, unusual, or irregular.
3. 'Anomalous' means deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected (Choice A).
4. 'Orthodox' (conventional), 'ubiquitous' (everywhere), and 'intuitive' (instinctive) fail the context.
explanationUz:
1. 'deviated markedly from normal' (odatiy me'yordan keskin farq qilgan) iborasi anomal, noodatiy ma'nosini talab qiladi.
2. 'Anomalous' so'zi to'g'ri keladi.
referenceFormula: \text{Context Clue: Deviated from Normal } \implies \text{ Anomalous}

prompt: As used in the text, what does the word 'lucid' most nearly mean?
passage: Professor Ramirez was renowned among her peers for converting convoluted quantum mechanics proofs into lucid explanations that even first-year undergraduates could comprehend with ease.
explanationEn:
1. The context states that first-year students could comprehend her explanations 'with ease' despite quantum mechanics being convoluted.
2. Therefore, 'lucid' means clear, plain, and readily intelligible (Choice A).
3. Choices B, C, and D do not fit the contextual meaning of clear communication.
explanationUz:
1. Kontekstda hatto 1-kurs talabalari ham tushunishi oson bo'lgani aytilgan.
2. Demak, 'lucid' so'zi ravshan, oson tushunarli ma'nosini bildiradi (A variant).
referenceFormula: \text{Context Clue: 'comprehend with ease'} \implies \text{lucid = clear}

prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?
passage: Although several engineers cautioned that the wooden footbridge was structurally unsound, local municipal authorities dismissed their concerns, claiming the structure was sufficiently _______ to endure another winter.
explanationEn:
1. The word 'Although' contrasts the engineers' warning that the bridge was 'unsound' with the authorities' claim that it could endure another winter.
2. Authorities therefore claimed it was sturdy or strong. 'Robust' means strong and healthy or vigorously sturdy (Choice B).
3. Fragile (A) and precarious (D) mean weak/unstable, contradicting the contrast; ornamental (C) means decorative.
explanationUz: 1. 'Although' qarama-qarshilik bildiradi: muhandislar ko'prik zaif deyishdi, ammo hokimiyat yana bir qishga chidash bera oladigan darajada mustahkam ('robust') deb hisobladi (B variant).
referenceFormula: \text{Contrast: 'unsound'} \iff \text{opposed by 'robust (strong)'}

prompt: While several contemporary biographers have lauded the prime minister for his resolute wartime leadership, recent archival declassifications suggest that his public confidence was carefully _______ by intense private doubts regarding military logistics.
explanationEn: In academic English, 'qualify' means to moderate, restrict, or make less extreme. The prime minister's public confidence was tempered or limited by his internal doubts.
explanationUz:
💡 MENTOR ESLATMASI (So'zlarning ikkilamchi akademik ma'nosi):
1. SAT'da so'zlarning oddiy ma'nosi emas, ikkilamchi akademik ma'nolari sinovdan o'tkaziladi.
2. 'Qualify' so'zi oddiy ingliz tilida 'malakaga ega bo'lish' bo'lsa, akademik ingliz tilida 'to limit, moderate, or make less absolute' (cheklash, mo''tadillashtirish, shubha ostiga qo'yish) ma'nosini beradi!
3. Matnda: Uning ommaviy ishonchi shaxsiy shubhalar tufayli to'liq bo'lmagan, ya'ni shubhalar uning ishonchini cheklab (qualified by doubts) turgan.
To'g'ri javob: B.
referenceFormula: \text{Qualify } = \text{ To limit or moderate an assertion}

prompt: While several contemporary biographers have lauded the prime minister for his resolute wartime leadership, recent archival declassifications suggest that his public confidence was carefully _______ by intense private doubts regarding military logistics.
explanationEn:
1. The sentence sets up a contrast between public praise for resolute confidence and internal private doubts.
2. The context clue indicates that his public confidence was not absolute; it was restrained or moderated by his internal doubts.
3. In advanced academic English, the verb **to qualify** means 'to limit, moderate, or make less absolute or extreme'.
4. Thus, his confidence was 'qualified' (tempered or restricted) by his private concerns.
5. 'Bolstered' means strengthened (the opposite of what doubts would do); 'precipitated' means caused suddenly.
explanationUz: SATda so'zlarning ikkilamchi ma'nolari sinovdan o'tkaziladi. 'Qualify' akademik ingliz tilida 'cheklash, mo'tadillashtirish' (to limit or moderate) ma'nosini beradi.
referenceFormula: \text{Qualify} = \text{To moderate, restrict, or limit an assertion}

prompt: In her lecture on renewable infrastructure, the civil engineer argued that intermittent renewable power sources cannot completely replace base-load coal generators unless municipal grids invest in ______ battery storage facilities.
explanationEn: The sentence requires an adjective describing large, sufficient battery facilities capable of meeting the heavy demands of an entire municipal grid. 'Substantial' means large in size, value, or importance. 'Obsolete' (outdated) contradicts progress; 'prolific' applies to creative output; 'capricious' (unpredictable) contradicts grid reliability. Choice C is correct. Source: Vocabook 3.0 (Page 48).
explanationUz: Shahar elektr tarmog'ini ta'minlash uchun batareya omborlari katta va yetarli hajmda bo'lishi kerak. 'Substantial' so'zi katta hajm va ahamiyatga ega degan ma'noni beradi. To'g'ri javob C. Manba: Vocabook 3.0 (48-bet).
desmosTrick: Context clue: 'completely replace base-load coal generators' requires large-scale storage -> Substantial.
referenceFormula: \text{Words in Context Precision}

prompt: Rather than offering empty platitudes, the independent ombudsman addressed the university senate with remarkable ______, detailing administrative lapses that contributed to the budget shortfall.
explanationEn: The sentence contrasts 'empty platitudes' with an honest, direct account of shortcomings. 'Candor' means openness, frankness, and honesty in speech. 'Reticence' (reluctance to speak) and 'ambiguity' (vagueness) contradict the thorough detailing of lapses. Choice B is correct. Source: Vocabook 3.0 (Page 88).
explanationUz: Gapda 'quruq gaplar' o'rniga kamchiliklarni ochiq-oydin aytganligi ta'kidlangan. 'Candor' - samimiylik, ochiqlik va haqiqatni yuzga aytish. To'g'ri javob B. Manba: Vocabook 3.0 (88-bet).
desmosTrick: Contrast clue: 'Rather than offering empty platitudes' -> Frank, honest speech -> Candor.
referenceFormula: \text{Words in Context Nuance}

prompt:
Text 1
Historians have long argued that early medieval iron bloomery technology was fundamentally inefficient, yielding low-grade wrought iron that required labor-intensive forging to expel trapped slag impurities. Consequently, the scale of military armament production in ninth-century Scandinavia was presumed to have been severely constrained by metallurgical limitations.

Text 2
Recent trace-element spectrometry of eighth- and ninth-century spearheads discovered near Hedeby reveals an extraordinarily homogeneous crystalline matrix with slag inclusions under 1.2% by volume. These findings demonstrate that Norse metallurgists possessed sophisticated thermal control techniques—manipulating blast furnace airflow via dual-chambered bellows—capable of producing high-carbon steel comparable to crucible iron from Damascus.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the historical consensus described in Text 1?
options: A. By acknowledging that while forging was labor-intensive, it nonetheless produced superior weapons.
B. By contending that physical evidence contradicts the assumption that metallurgical limitations curtailed weapon production quality.
C. By arguing that Hedeby was an atypical trade emporium that imported all of its steel from the Near East.
D. By suggesting that Scandinavian smiths prioritized spearhead aesthetics over structural durability.
explanationEn: Text 1 states that medieval bloomery was presumed 'fundamentally inefficient' and 'severely constrained' armament production. Text 2 presents physical archaeological findings (trace-element spectrometry) showing Norse metallurgists had sophisticated thermal control producing high-carbon steel with minimal slag. Thus, the author of Text 2 directly challenges the traditional consensus cited in Text 1 by showing physical evidence contradicts the presumed limitations (Choice B). Source: SAToplam Reading Book.
explanationUz: 1-matnda qadimgi temirchilik texnologiyasi past sifatli bo'lgan deb taxmin qilingan. 2-matn esa eng yangi spektral tahlillar orqali Skandinaviya temirchilari yuqori uglerodli po'lat ishlab chiqarganini isbotlaydi. Demak, 2-matn muallifi 1-matndagi an'anaviy taxminni rad etadi (B). Manba: SAToplam Reading Book.
desmosTrick: Cross-text synthesis: identify the core claim in Text 1 (inefficient metallurgy), then identify how Text 2 refutes it with empirical spectrometry data.
referenceFormula: Text 2 Evidence contradicts Text 1 Consensus

prompt:
Text 1
Classical economic theory posits that consumer choices are governed by utility maximization: individuals systematically weigh marginal costs against expected benefits before arriving at an equilibrium decision. When faced with an expanding array of product options, rational consumers should experience greater welfare, as the probability of locating an optimal match increases monotonically.

Text 2
Psychologist Barry Schwartz and behavioral economists have documented that extensive choice menus frequently induce 'choice paralysis' and elevated post-purchase regret. When subject to hundreds of permutations, the cognitive burden of evaluating marginal trade-offs overwhelms executive working memory, causing individuals to either abandon the purchase entirely or report diminished satisfaction with their ultimate selection.

Based on the texts, how does Text 2 complicate the perspective advanced in Text 1?
options: A. It establishes that consumers are incapable of understanding basic pricing mechanisms.
B. It demonstrates that expanding choice sets can paradoxically decrease consumer welfare by imposing excessive cognitive burdens.
C. It proves that utility maximization applies exclusively to non-commercial financial decisions.
D. It confirms that consumers invariably select the lowest-priced alternative when confused.
explanationEn: Text 1 asserts that more choices monotonically increase consumer welfare under rational utility maximization. Text 2 introduces empirical behavioral evidence that extensive choices cause 'choice paralysis', regret, and cognitive overload, leading to diminished satisfaction. Hence, Text 2 shows that expanding choice sets paradoxically decreases welfare (Choice B). Source: SAToplam Reading Book.
explanationUz: 1-matn tanlov ko'p bo'lsa inson manfaati oshadi deb ta'kidlaydi. 2-matn esa psixologik tadqiqotlar asosida ortiqcha tanlov inson miyasini charchatib, qoniqishni pasaytirishini (paradoks) ko'rsatadi (B). Manba: SAToplam Reading Book.
desmosTrick: Identify paradox: Text 1 says 'more options = more welfare', Text 2 shows 'more options = cognitive overload and lower satisfaction'.
referenceFormula: Paradox of Choice Heuristic

prompt: In observational astronomy, Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) represent exceptionally ______ phenomena: lasting a mere few milliseconds, these colossal pulses of coherent radio emission discharge more energy than the Sun generates over several decades before vanishing entirely into cosmic silence.
explanationEn: The colon introduces the clue: 'lasting a mere few milliseconds... before vanishing entirely'. 'Ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time; fleeting or transient. 'Immutable' means unchangeable; 'perfunctory' means carried out with minimal effort; 'mundane' means ordinary. Only 'ephemeral' matches (Choice B). Source: Vocabook 3.0 (Page 42, Set 4).
explanationUz: Matnda portlash bir necha millisekund davom etishi ('lasting a mere few milliseconds') va darhol g'oyib bo'lishi aytilgan. Bu juda qisqa umr ko'ruvchi, o'tkinchi degan ma'nodagi 'ephemeral' so'ziga to'liq mos keladi (B). Manba: Vocabook 3.0.
desmosTrick: Context clue: 'lasting a mere few milliseconds... vanishing entirely' = ephemeral (fleeting).
referenceFormula: Contextual Connotation Matching

prompt: Recognizing that uncoordinated monetary tightening could ______ an acute liquidity crisis across emerging markets, central bank governors convened an emergency multilateral summit to synchronize overnight lending rate adjustments.
explanationEn: The governors convened because uncoordinated tightening could cause or bring about a crisis. 'Precipitate' as a verb means to cause (an event, typically undesirable) to happen suddenly, unexpectedly, or prematurely. 'Mitigate' means to alleviate/lessen; 'belie' means to contradict; 'vacillate' means to waver. Only 'precipitate' fits (Choice A). Source: Vocabook 3.0 (Page 88, Set 8).
explanationUz: Hukumat vakillari shoshilinch yig'ilish o'tkazishdi, chunki noaniq choralar inqirozni keltirib chiqarishi (boshlab berishi) mumkin edi. 'Precipitate' - kutilmagan salbiy hodisani tezlashtirish/keltirib chiqarish deganidir (A). Manba: Vocabook 3.0.
desmosTrick: Cause-effect verb: 'uncoordinated tightening could [cause/bring about] crisis' = precipitate.
referenceFormula: High-Register Vocabulary Trigger

prompt: Excavating the subterranean chambers of Pompeii required ______ attention to detail: archaeologists meticulously brushed away cubic centimeters of volcanic ash with camel-hair tools to preserve the fragile plaster casts of ancient organic remains.
explanationEn: The clue is 'meticulously brushed away cubic centimeters... with camel-hair tools to preserve'. 'Fastidious' means very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail; meticulous. 'Capricious' means whimsical/unpredictable; 'dogmatic' means rigidly opinionated; 'reticent' means reserved/uncommunicative. Only 'fastidious' fits (Choice A). Source: Vocabook 3.0 (Page 112, Set 11).
explanationUz: Arxeologlar santimetrlab kulni yumshoq cho'tka bilan o'ta ehtiyotkorlik bilan tozalashgan. 'Fastidious' - mayda detallargacha nihoyatda sinchkov, ehtiyotkor demakdir (A). Manba: Vocabook 3.0.
desmosTrick: Synonym matching: 'meticulous brushing with camel-hair tools' = fastidious attention.
referenceFormula: Contextual Synonym Matching

prompt:
Before the 1847 introduction of the US postage stamp, the cost of postage was usually paid by the recipient of a letter rather
than the sender, and recipients were not always able or willing to pay promptly. ______ collecting this fee could be slow and
arduous, and heaps of unpaid-for, undeliverable mail piled up in post offices.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanationEn:
Choice C is the best answer. “Consequently” logically signals that the postal problems described in this sentence
(slow fee collection, heaps of undeliverable mail) were a consequence of the fee system described in the previous
sentence.

here. Instead, these two examples work together to support the claim made in the rst sentence. Choice C is
incorrect. This choice uses a transition that indicates the addition of an agreeing idea. But these two examples are

prompt: The student wants to emphasize the difference in the primary dietary sources of the two penguin species. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Adélie penguin (*Pygoscelis adeliae*) breeds along the coast of the Antarctic continent.
• Its diet primarily consists of Antarctic krill.
• The gentoo penguin (*Pygoscelis papua*) inhabits sub-Antarctic islands and the Antarctic Peninsula.
• Its diet consists mainly of fish, squid, and crustaceans in varying proportions.
• Both species are taxonomically classified under the genus *Pygoscelis*.
options: A. Although both belong to the genus Pygoscelis, the Adélie penguin feeds almost exclusively on Antarctic krill, whereas the gentoo penguin's diet is more diverse, comprising fish and squid alongside crustaceans.
B. Belonging to the genus Pygoscelis, the Adélie penguin and gentoo penguin inhabit distinct Antarctic and sub-Antarctic geographical regions.
C. The diet of the gentoo penguin consists mainly of fish, squid, and crustaceans, which it hunts across sub-Antarctic waters.
D. Antarctic krill constitutes the primary nutritional staple for Adélie penguins living along the Antarctic coast.
explanationEn:
1. Target Goal: 'emphasize the difference in the primary dietary sources of the two penguin species'.
2. Constraint Checklist: Must mention BOTH species, and must directly CONTRAST their diets.
3. Choice A compares both diets ('almost exclusively on Antarctic krill, whereas the gentoo penguin's diet is more diverse').
4. Choices B, C, and D fail the specific prompt constraint by omitting diet contrast or omitting one species.
explanationUz:
1. Savol maqsadi: ikkala turning OZUQA FARQINI ko'rsatish.
2. A variant ikkala turni ham, ularning ozuqa farqini ham ('whereas...') to'liq ochib bergan.
referenceFormula: \text{Goal Matching: Both Subjects + Contrast in Target Property}

prompt: The student wants to introduce Henrietta Swan Leavitt's key astronomical contribution to an audience unfamiliar with variable stars. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Henrietta Swan Leavitt was an American astronomer working at Harvard College Observatory in the early 1900s.
• She examined photographic glass plates of the Small Magellanic Cloud.
• She discovered a direct mathematical relationship between the period of a Cepheid variable star's brightness fluctuations and its intrinsic luminosity.
• Her period-luminosity relation became the 'standard candle' astronomers used to measure interstellar and intergalactic distances.
options: A. Working at Harvard College Observatory, American astronomer Henrietta Swan Leavitt discovered a relationship between a Cepheid star's pulsation period and its brightness, providing astronomers with a benchmark to calculate cosmic distances.
B. Henrietta Swan Leavitt studied photographic glass plates of the Small Magellanic Cloud in the early 1900s.
C. In the early 1900s, photographic glass plates were standard tools utilized by female human computers at Harvard.
D. Measuring interstellar distances had long puzzled astronomers until twentieth-century computational techniques emerged.
explanationEn:
1. Prompt goal: 'introduce Henrietta Swan Leavitt's key astronomical contribution to an audience unfamiliar with variable stars'.
2. Choice A clearly identifies Leavitt, explains what she discovered (period-luminosity relationship), and why it matters (benchmark to measure cosmic distances).
3. Choices B, C, and D fail to introduce her fundamental discovery and its broad astronomical significance.
explanationUz:
1. Maqsad: Henrietta Leavittning asosiy ilmiy hissasini yangi o'quvchiga tanishtirish.
2. A variant uning kashfiyotini (davr va yorqinlik bog'liqligi) hamda uning olam masofalarini o'lchashdagi ahamiyatini to'liq ifodalaydi.
referenceFormula: \text{Goal: Introduce Person + Specific Discovery + Real-World Impact}

prompt: The student wants to explain how acoustic architects designed the concert hall to control reverberation time. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Reverberation time is the duration required for sound pressure to decrease by 60 decibels after the sound source ceases.
• Symphony orchestras perform best in concert halls with reverberation times between 1.8 and 2.2 seconds.
• To achieve this ideal acoustics in Tokyo Opera City Concert Hall, architects installed pyramid-shaped wooden ceiling baffles.
• The baffles disperse high-frequency sound waves evenly while dense wool-felt wall panels absorb excessive low-frequency resonance.
options: A. Tokyo Opera City Concert Hall features pyramid-shaped ceiling baffles to diffuse high frequencies and dense wool-felt wall panels to absorb low-frequency resonance, thereby achieving an ideal reverberation time for orchestral performance.
B. Reverberation time measures the duration required for sound pressure to decrease by 60 decibels after a sound stops.
C. Architects in Tokyo often construct concert halls using natural wood and wool-felt textiles.
D. Symphony orchestras prefer performing in spaces with reverberation times between 1.8 and 2.2 seconds rather than shorter intervals.
explanationEn:
1. Prompt goal: 'explain HOW acoustic architects designed the concert hall to control reverberation time'.
2. Choice A explains the exact architectural mechanism: pyramid ceiling baffles for high frequencies + wool-felt panels for low frequencies to achieve ideal reverberation.
3. Choices B, C, and D state isolated facts without explaining HOW architects controlled reverberation.
explanationUz:
1. Maqsad: me'morlar aks-sado vaqtini NAZORAT QILISH UCHUN NIMA QILGANINI tushuntirish.
2. A variant piramida shaklidagi ship panellari va kigiz devorlar orqali bu qanday amalga oshirilganini to'liq ifodalaydi.
referenceFormula: \text{Goal: Architectural Mechanism (How) } \to \text{ Acoustic Control Outcome}

explanationEn: Option A directly satisfies the goal by contrasting both species' diets. Options B, C, and D fail the specific prompt constraint.
explanationUz: QADAM 1 (IELTS 7.5 talabasi uchun SAT qoidasi): Savol maqsadini (goal) tekshiring: 'emphasize the difference in the primary dietary sources of the two penguin species'.
